title: Widen the model: d_model 256 -> 320 with 10 heads of 32 (6.23M params, cap 10M) on the 081 Polar Express Muon incumbent
description: Width axis of P24/P25 (capacity within the unchanged 10M cap; no backlog entry scales width alone): every matrix grows 1.25x per side (d_model 320, 10 heads keeping head dim 32, d_ff 1280), 4.00M -> 6.23M params, all optimizer settings unchanged. Depth changes (051 keep, 062/057 noise) were tested but width never was under Muon; a wider residual stream gives RL's fixed AdamW more directions to adapt without adding sequential kernels, so sampling should stay roughly as fast as depth-5.
hypothesis: Pretraining loss is saturated (~0.09 val, 0.99 greedy) and the metric depends on how well expert iteration extends proofs past 6 lines. A wider model under Muon's spectral update (spectral norm per step unchanged by width, so the LR transfers) stores the same cap-6 skills in a higher-dimensional, less superposed representation, which should let RL's AdamW updates add longer-proof behaviour with less interference, and larger models are generally more sample-efficient learners. Cost: ~1.56x matmul FLOPs, but pretraining steps are launch/overhead-bound (~10% A40 utilization at 16 steps/s), so steps should fall only ~10-25% and RL sampling (062 showed +20% depth cost only ~5% RL wall-clock) should slow by <10%.
expected_delta: -50 to +50 on the 3-seed mean (central guess 0); pretraining steps 3600-4400 vs 4682-4769, final val loss within +-0.005 of 081's 0.095/0.091/0.096, total_secs 1110-1180 vs ~1095 (timeout risk if RL slows >10%)

arch.change: CHANGED versus 081-claude: d_model 256 -> 320 and heads 8 -> 10 so head dim stays 32; d_ff follows the fork's 4*d_model (1024 -> 1280). Still 5 untied fork GPT blocks, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 320, 10) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5, d=320, n_head=10
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D now 320 (the formula references the width constant, unchanged code): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2, head (99,320) 1. Every Muon update keeps element RMS ~1/sqrt(D) times lr, i.e. each square hidden matrix still gets an orthogonal update of spectral norm ~lr (muP-consistent spectral scale), element RMS 1/17.9 instead of 1/16
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,320) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (960,320) use independent Q/K/V updates as a batch of three (320,320) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: orthogonal hidden block matrices with element RMS 0.02 (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(shape))), unchanged from 081; embeddings/head/LayerNorm fork default (normal 0.02)
